newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Ministers may agree satellite fish controls on Monday.
newsitem.headline: Ministers may agree satellite fish controls on Monday.

text.p: Fisheries ministers may reach political agreement on Monday on a satellite system for monitoring fishing vessels, diplomats said.
The agreement can only be finalised after the European Parliament has given its opinion.
Ministers still have to resolve differences over start-up dates, type of vessels covered and funding.
The Commission has proposed to start the system for vessels fishing in non-EU waters, industrial fishing and driftnets over one km in length from January 1997.
The system would be extended to all vessels with an overall length of more than 18 metres from January 1999.
However several member states, including Britain, say only larger vessels of more than 24 metres should be covered and that the start-up dates should be delayed.
Some countries say that funding should only be tackled when all the details have been settled.
Under the system, satellites will track vessels' movements and transmit the information to their home countries which will then pass it onto the country in whose waters they are fishing.
Pilot projects between July 1994 and December 1995 showed that satellites considerably strengthened fishing controls, the Commission said.
